title: Counit normalization of the first localization-triangle component
statement:
Let $\mathcal T_A,\mathcal T_B$ be pre-triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category], $\mathcal C_A,\mathcal C_B$ categories, and $I_R:\mathcal C_R\to\mathcal T_R$ left adjoint to $J_R$, with counit $\epsilon_R$, for $R=A,B$. Adjunction means natural Hom-set bijections with unit, counit and triangle identities [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Assume $I_B$ is fully faithful, meaning it induces bijections on Hom sets. Let $S_X:\mathcal T_A\to\mathcal T_B$ be an exact functor, $S_Z:\mathcal C_A\to\mathcal C_B$ a functor, and $c:S_XI_A\xrightarrow{\sim}I_BS_Z$ a natural isomorphism. For an object $M\in\mathcal T_A$, suppose given distinguished triangles
$$I_AJ_AM\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{A,M}}M\xrightarrow{\eta_A}L_A\longrightarrow,$$
$$I_BJ_BS_XM\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{B,S_XM}}S_XM\xrightarrow{\eta_B}L_B\longrightarrow,$$
and an isomorphism $d:S_XL_A\xrightarrow{\sim}L_B$ with $dS_X(\eta_A)=\eta_B$. Let $b:S_ZJ_AM\to J_BS_XM$ be the adjoint of $S_X(\epsilon_{A,M})c_{J_AM}^{-1}$. There exists a morphism of distinguished triangles from the $S_X$-image of the first triangle to the second, with second component $1_{S_XM}$ and third component $d$. Its first component $a$ is an isomorphism and is uniquely determined by
$$\epsilon_{B,S_XM}a=S_X(\epsilon_{A,M}).$$
It satisfies $a c_{J_AM}^{-1}=I_B(b)$. These assertions identify the first component of every such triangle morphism with the image of the prescribed adjunction transpose.

proof.text: Write the $S_X$-image triangle as $U\xrightarrow{e}V\xrightarrow{v}W\xrightarrow{w}U[1]$ and the second triangle as $U'\xrightarrow{e'}V\xrightarrow{v'}W'\xrightarrow{w'}U'[1]$: explicitly $U=S_XI_AJ_AM$, $V=S_XM$, $W=S_XL_A$, $U'=I_BJ_BV$, $W'=L_B$, and target arrows $e'=\epsilon_{B,V},v'=\eta_B,w'$. The source is distinguished by exactness of $S_X$, using its specified shift comparison in $w$. Rotate both triangles by TR2 and apply TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to $(1_V,d)$, since $dv=v'$. This gives $h:U[1]\to U'[1]$ with $hw=w' d$ and $(-e'[1])h=(-e[1])$. Full faithfulness of the shift autoequivalence gives a unique $a:U\to U'$ with $a[1]=h$. Additivity and faithfulness of shift turn the latter equation into $e' a=e$. Thus $(a,1_V,d)$ is a morphism of the original distinguished triangles.

source.place: Tag 0145, definition-triangulated-category, TR2 and TR3; explicit rotated completion

proof.text: Both $1_V$ and $d$ are isomorphisms. Apply [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] to the morphism constructed in step 1: its first component $a$ is an isomorphism. Only pre-triangulatedness is required.

Put $P=S_ZJ_AM$, $Q=J_BV$, $c_0=c_{J_AM}:U\xrightarrow{\sim}I_BP$ and $\phi=e c_0^{-1}:I_BP\to V$. For any $t:U\to I_BQ$ with $\epsilon_{B,V}t=e$, fullness of $I_B$ gives $f:P\to Q$ with $I_B(f)=t c_0^{-1}$. Hence $\epsilon_{B,V}I_B(f)=\phi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], $f=J_B(\phi)\nu_P$, where $\nu$ denotes the adjunction unit. This is precisely the prescribed adjunct $b$. Thus every such $t$ equals $I_B(b)c_0$. Taking $t=a$ proves $a c_0^{-1}=I_B(b)$ and uniqueness among all morphisms satisfying the displayed counit equation. The first component of every triangle morphism with middle component $1_V$ satisfies that equation by its first square, so it is this same invertible $a$.

Step 1: the TR2 rotation (sign -u[1]) and TR3 on (1_V,d) give h; since the shift is an additive automorphism, h=a[1] and e'a=e. All three squares commute, including the connecting one. Step 2: two-out-of-three, which needs only pre-triangulated categories. Step 3: fullness gives f with I_B f = t c0^{-1} and ε I_B f = e c0^{-1} = φ. The adjunct-counit equivalence forces f=b, which gives the identity a c^{-1}=I_B(b), uniqueness, and that the first component of every (a',1,d) equals a; elementary is justified. I checked the Hom shapes and the edge cases M=0 and the identity adjunction. Fullness of I_B is needed for uniqueness. The use in the parent's step 2 matches exactly. No SGA source is used; the cited nodes are Mathlib leaves or definitions, so no tool_uses are needed. Minor: the report mentions a citations.json that is not in the commit; not a fault.
